summaries.intro_en: ✧ Covers the beginning of creation, the heavens, the Throne, angels, jinn, Satan, and the stories of the prophets from Adam to Jesus and earlier peoples, concluding with a compendium of past prophets.
✧ Describes the creation of the earth as part of the creation of the heavens and the earth.
✧ Presents accounts of the Throne, the Footstool, and the Preserved Tablet, including their descriptions, bearers, and scriptural evidences.
✧ Discusses the creation of angels from light, their attributes, various categories, duties, and the debated question of their superiority over humans.
✧ Relates the creation of the jinn from fire, their types, beliefs, and the story of Iblīs, his fall, enmity toward Adam's progeny, and the means to seek protection from him.
✧ Narrates the creation of Adam from clay, the angels' prostration, Iblīs's refusal, Adam's dwelling in Paradise, his descent, progeny, the killing of Abel, and his death and burial.
✧ Tells the story of Idrīs, identified with Enoch, the first to write and sew, his prophethood, and his being raised to a high station.
✧ Covers the story of Noah, his call, the Flood, and his attributes and character with his Lord.

✧ Covers Ḥūd’s lineage, his mission to the first ʿĀd and their idol worship, their denial of him, and their destruction by wind, his salvation and death, with Qurʾānic accounts and their interpretation.
✧ Relates Ṣāliḥ’s lineage, his call to the idolatrous Thamūd, the sign of the she-camel, its hamstringing by Qudār b. Sālif, their destruction by the shout and earthquake, and Ṣāliḥ’s later life.
✧ Deals with Abraham’s description and virtues, the story of Lot, and the story of Shuʿayb.
✧ Covers the stories of Abraham’s offspring: Ishmael, Isaac, Joseph, Job, and Dhū al-Kifl.
✧ Discusses nations destroyed en masse, including the People of al-Rass and the People of Yā Sīn, with their prophets and destruction.
✧ Recounts Jonah’s mission to Nineveh, his departure and swallowing by the whale, his supplication and deliverance, and the belief of his people.
✧ Details Moses’ story, including al-Khiḍr’s genealogy and meeting with Moses, and Yūshaʿ b. Nūn’s prophethood and leadership over the Israelites.
✧ Discusses Ilyās’s lineage, his prophetic mission against the worship of Baʿl, his conflict with the king and people, and his departure from them.
✧ A group of Israelite prophets after Mūsā includes Ḥizqīl, al-Yasaʿ, and Ashmūʾīl, whose stories are recounted in brief.
✧ The story of Dāwūd covers his lineage, killing of Jālūt, kingship and prophethood, miracles, Psalms, worship, wisdom, litigants, wives, building of Bayt al-Maqdis, and death.
✧ Sulaymān b. Dāwūd's genealogy and the miracles God granted him are presented.

✧ Stories of Israelite prophets after Dāwūd and Sulaymān and before Zakariyyā and Yaḥyā, including Shaʿyā b. Amṣiyā, Armiyā b. Ḥalqiyā, Dāniyāl, the destruction of Jerusalem, the building of the Sacred House, and ʿUzayr.
✧ The story of ʿUzayr, his lineage, whether he was a prophet, God causing him to die for a hundred years, his revival, and his renewal of the Torah for the Children of Israel.
✧ The lives of the prophets Zakariyyā and his son Yaḥyā, including their prophethood and roles among the Israelites.
✧ The story of ʿĪsā b. Maryam from Maryam's pregnancy and his birth through his qualities, virtues, miracles, and significant events in his time.
✧ Accounts of past peoples from the Israelites and others encompass the stories of Dhū al-Qarnayn and Yaʾjūj and Maʾjūj, the Companions of the Cave, the owner of the two gardens, and Luqmān.
✧ Reports of the number, crafts, tribulations, sacred laws, and common religion of earlier prophets are gathered, along with narrations about their years and those born circumcised.
✧ The Prophetic biography covers the genealogy, birth, upbringing, call, emigration, expeditions, treaties, farewell pilgrimage, and death of Muḥammad ﷺ, followed by the accession of Abū Bakr.
✧ This chapter surveys the origins and genealogies of the Arabs, the advent of idol worship, pre-Islamic accounts, the virtues of Zamzam, and notable figures of the Jāhiliyyah.
✧ Accounts of Āminah's death and burial at al-Abwāʾ, the Prophet's ﷺ grief over her grave, and his grandfather ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib's tender guardianship until his own death are related.
✧ The birth of Muḥammad ﷺ, its remarkable signs, his naming, suckling by Thuwaybah and Ḥalīmah, the splitting of his chest, and his return to his mother are recounted.
✧ Abū Ṭālib's guardianship of the Prophet ﷺ, his loving care, the monk Baḥīrā's recognition, divine protection from idolatry, and Abū Ṭālib's prayer for rain through him are narrated.
✧ Khadījah's proposal to the Prophet ﷺ at age twenty-five, the circumstances of their marriage, dowry, children, and Waraqah's confirmation of his prophethood are detailed.
✧ Quraysh's reconstruction of the Kaʿbah, the discovery of its foundations, the dispute over placing the Black Stone, and the Prophet's ﷺ arbitration are recounted.
✧ Quraysh and allied tribes adopted the Ḥums, abandoning certain pilgrimage rites and imposing strict taboos on food, tents, and circumambulation garments until Islam abrogated these innovations.

✧ Reports from Jewish rabbis, Christian monks, and Arab soothsayers announced the coming of the Prophet ﷺ, including accounts of Salmān al-Fārisī, Waraqah b. Nawfal, and the jinn being barred from hearing.
✧ The section covers the beginning of the Prophet's ﷺ mission, including the virtues of Khadījah ؓ.
✧ The earliest converts to Islam included Khadījah, ʿAlī b. Abī Ṭālib, Zayd b. Ḥārithah, and Abū Bakr, followed by many others whom Abū Bakr brought to the faith, and later Ḥamzah.

✧ The Prophet ﷺ openly proclaimed Islam, and Quraysh repeatedly tried to restrain him through Abū Ṭālib, agreed to call him a sorcerer, and persecuted the believers while the Prophet ﷺ received divine protection.

✧ Quraysh's leaders offered the Prophet ﷺ wealth, kingship, or healing, then questioned him about the Companions of the Cave, Dhū al-Qarnayn, and the Spirit, leading to the revelation of Sūrat al-Kahf.

✧ The Prophet ﷺ endured harm from polytheists such as Abū Lahab, Umayyah b. Khalaf, al-ʿĀṣ b. Wāʾil, al-Naḍr b. al-Ḥārith, al-Akhnas b. Sharīq, al-Walīd b. al-Mughīrah, Ubayy b. Khalaf, and ʿUqbah b. Abī Muʿayṭ, with corresponding revelations.

✧ Allah sufficed the Prophet ﷺ against the mockers by inflicting blindness, dropsy, and other afflictions on al-Aswad b. al-Muṭṭalib, al-Aswad b. ʿAbd Yaghūth, al-Walīd b. al-Mughīrah, al-ʿĀṣ b. Wāʾil, and al-Ḥārith b. al-Ṭulāṭilah.
✧ It recounts Quraysh's torture of early Muslims, including ʿAbd Allāh b. Masʿūd's public recitation, Bilāl's endurance, Abū Bakr's freeing of slaves, and the martyrdom of Sumayyah and Yāsir.
✧ It narrates the Muslim emigration to Abyssinia, the Negus's protection and conversion, Quraysh's failed envoys, the Najāshī's rise to power, and the emigrants' eventual return.
✧ It details ʿUmar b. al-Khaṭṭāb's conversion through hearing the Qurʾān, his strength in Islam, and the story of the boycott document and its annulment.
✧ It recounts how Abū Jahl withheld payment from a man of Irāsh, the Prophet ﷺ secured justice, and Abū Jahl feared a stallion of camels above the Prophet's head.
✧ It covers the account of the pact among Quraysh to boycott Banū Hāshim and the believers, and its eventual annulment.
✧ It concerns the Prophet ﷺ's frown at Ibn Umm Maktūm, the revelation of Sūrat ʿAbasa, and Ibn Umm Maktūm's subsequent honor and deputyships.
✧ It narrates how al-Ṭufayl b. ʿAmr al-Dawsī ignored Quraysh's warnings, heard the Prophet ﷺ, received a light as a sign, and converted his family and tribe.
✧ It recounts a Christian delegation from Abyssinia embracing Islam, Abū Jahl's mockery, and Qurʾānic verses revealed concerning them and the weak believers.
✧ It covers the signs the Messenger of Allah ﷺ witnessed during the Night Journey and Ascension.
✧ It recounts the increased harm by Quraysh after the deaths of Abū Ṭālib and Khadījah, including the Prophet's ﷺ journey to al-Ṭāʾif and his rejection by Thaqīf.
✧ It describes the Messenger of Allah's ﷺ efforts to present himself to various Arab tribes at fairs, seeking support and protection.
✧ It details the first pledge of al-ʿAqabah, the acceptance of Islam by six men from al-Khazraj, and Muṣʿab b. ʿUmayr's missionary work in Madinah.
✧ It covers the second pledge of al-ʿAqabah, where seventy-three men and two women pledged to protect the Prophet ﷺ, including the appointment of twelve naqībs.
✧ It narrates the Prophet's ﷺ emigration from Makkah to Madinah with Abū Bakr, their stay in the cave, encounters along the way, and initial settlement and mosque construction in Madinah.
✧ It recounts interactions between the Prophet ﷺ and the Jews, Christians, and hypocrites of Madinah, including their questions, opposition, and selected conversions.
✧ It details the fever that afflicted the Emigrants in Madinah and the Prophet's ﷺ supplication to transfer its pestilence to al-Juḥfah.

✧ This section narrates the beginning of fighting after the Hijrah, including the revelation of permission to fight, the start of expeditions, and scholarly accounts of the Prophet’s ﷺ expeditions, detachments, and their numbers.
✧ The first expedition of the Prophet ﷺ to al-Abwāʾ or Waddān in the second year AH, to intercept a Quraysh caravan, ending in a treaty with Banū Ḍamrah.
✧ The detachment of ʿUbayda b. al-Ḥārith to Baṭn Rābigh, the first banner tied by the Prophet ﷺ, involving a skirmish with Abū Sufyān and the defection of two Muslims.
✧ The detachment of Ḥamza b. ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib to the seacoast, where he intercepted a Quraysh caravan led by Abū Jahl, but Majdī b. ʿAmr al-Juhanī intervened to prevent fighting.
✧ The Prophet’s ﷺ expedition to Buwāṭ in the second year AH, to intercept a Quraysh caravan led by Umayyah b. Khalaf, which ended without battle.
✧ The expedition to al-ʿUshayra, where the Prophet ﷺ attempted to intercept a Quraysh caravan bound for Syria, and ʿAlī b. Abī Ṭālib received the kunyah Abū Turāb.
✧ A detachment led by Saʿd b. Abī Waqqāṣ to al-Khazzāz near Baṭn Rābigh, tasked with intercepting a Quraysh caravan that had already passed.
✧ The Prophet’s ﷺ pursuit of Kurz b. Jābir al-Fihrī after his raid on Madinah’s camels, reaching Safawān but failing to catch him.
✧ ʿAbd Allāh b. Jaḥsh led eight Emigrants in the second year to Nakhla, where they seized a Quraysh caravan, killed ʿAmr b. al-Ḥaḍramī, took captives and booty, and were justified by revealed verses.
✧ The Great Battle of Badr on 17 Ramaḍān year 2 resulted in a decisive Muslim victory over Quraysh, with detailed accounts of its causes, participants, combats, captives, spoils, and aftermath.
✧ The Prophet ﷺ marched against Banū Sulaym at al-Kudr, found their encampments empty, seized five hundred camels and a shepherd, then returned and distributed the spoils.
✧ Abū Sufyān raided Madinah's outskirts, killed two men, and fled; the Prophet ﷺ pursued him but recovered only abandoned sawīq provisions.
✧ The Prophet ﷺ led an expedition against Ghaṭafān at Dhū Amarr; his life was threatened by Duʿthūr, who then embraced Islam, and the enemy fled without battle.
✧ The Prophet ﷺ marched to Buḥrān with three hundred men after learning of a Banū Sulaym gathering, but they dispersed, and he returned without hostilities.
✧ Banū Qaynuqāʿ broke their pact with the Prophet ﷺ, were besieged and expelled from Madinah, and their wealth was distributed as spoils.
✧ Zayd b. Ḥāritha led a detachment that intercepted a Quraysh caravan at al-Qarada, capturing booty and Furāt b. Ḥayyān, who converted to Islam.
✧ Muḥammad b. Maslama and several Anṣārī companions kill the Jewish poet Kaʿb b. al-Ashraf for his insults and incitement after Badr.
✧ Ḥuwayyiṣa b. Masʿūd embraces Islam after his brother Muḥayyiṣa kills a Jew on the Prophet's order.
✧ The Meccan polytheists march out to avenge Badr, and the subsequent battle of Uḥud tests the believers with setback and loss.
✧ A group of Muslims sent to ʿAḍal and al-Qārah is betrayed, leading to the martyrdom of ʿĀṣim, Khubayb, and Zayd.
✧ Seventy Qurʾān reciters are treacherously slain at Biʾr Maʿūnah after being sent to Najd under Abū Barāʾ's protection.
✧ Banū al-Naḍīr's plot to kill the Prophet leads to their siege, surrender, and expulsion to Khaybar, with their lands distributed.
✧ The Prophet leads an expedition to Najd against Ghatafān, where the prayer of fear is instituted and a miraculous sign occurs.
✧ The Muslims march to Badr to meet Abū Sufyān's promised battle, but the polytheists turn back, and the Muslims profit at the fair.
✧ Describes the Expedition of Dūmat al-Jandal in year five, its cause, the raid on grazing livestock and herdsmen, the truce with ʿUyaynah b. Ḥiṣn, and the Prophet's ﷺ return to Madinah.
✧ Focuses on the miracles that appeared during the Expedition of al-Khandaq (the Confederates).
✧ Covers the account of Abū Lubābah and the revelation concerning him, and the killing of Banū Qurayẓah, seizure of their property, and captivity of their women and children.
✧ Relates the detachment of ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿAtīk against Abū Rāfiʿ Sallām b. Abī al-Ḥuqayq al-Naḍrī, including the killing and its aftermath.
✧ Narrates the conversions of ʿAmr b. al-ʿĀṣ, Khālid b. al-Walīd, and ʿUthmān b. Ṭalḥah, including their journeys and pledges of allegiance to the Prophet ﷺ.
✧ Details the Expedition of Banū Liḥyān in year six, including its cause, the Prophet's ﷺ route, the prayer of fear revelation, and his visit to his mother's grave.
✧ Describes the Expedition of Dhū Qarad (al-Ghabah), including the raid on the Prophet's ﷺ milch-camels, the pursuit, recovery of spoils, and the return to Madinah.
✧ Addresses Ibn Ubayy's stance on the quarrel between Jahjah and Sinan during the Expedition of Banū al-Muṣṭaliq (al-Muraysīʿ).
✧ It covers the Pledge of Riḍwān, the plight of the oppressed believers after the truce, and the case of emigrant women.
✧ It recounts the conquest of Khaybar, including the fortresses taken, the killing of Marḥab, the marriage to Ṣafiyyah, the poisoned sheep, and the distribution of spoils.
✧ It describes the return of Jaʿfar b. Abī Ṭālib and the Abyssinian emigrants, their reception by the Prophet ﷺ, and the names of those who came back aor died there.
✧ It narrates the compensatory ʿUmrah in year seven, including the entry into Makkah, the ramal, the marriage to Maymūnah, and the custody of Ḥamzah's daughter.
✧ It deals with the encounter with the Byzantines at Muʾtah.
✧ It deals with the causes of the greatest conquest, the conquest of Makkah.
✧ It recounts Khālid b. al-Walīd's detachment to Banū Jadhīmah, where he killed captives, the Prophet's disavowal, the compensation paid, and the poems exchanged.
✧ It describes Khālid b. al-Walīd's demolition of al-ʿUzzā, his initial incomplete destruction, and his second return when he killed the black woman who represented the idol.
✧ Covers the Prophet's ﷺ departure to fight Hawāzin, the battle events, divine protection, signs of prophethood, the fate of the polytheists, and poetry about the expedition.

✧ Details the Prophet's ﷺ ʿumrah from al-Jiʿrānah in Dhū al-Qaʿdah year 8, his return to Madinah, delegation of authority over Makkah to ʿAttāb b. Usayd, and scholarly discussion of his four post-Hijrah ʿumrahs.
✧ Narrates the events of the Tabūk expedition from the Prophet's ﷺ departure until his return.
✧ Recounts the Thaqīf delegation's arrival in Ramaḍān year 9, their negotiation and conversion, the appointment of ʿUthmān b. Abī al-ʿĀṣ, and the demolition of the idol al-Lāt.
✧ Describes Abū Bakr's leadership of the pilgrimage and the revelation of Sūrat Barāʾah.
✧ Covers the delegations of Banū Tamīm, Banū ʿĀmir, and various Yemeni tribes that came to the Prophet ﷺ in year nine, including the revelation of Sūrat al-Ḥujurāt.
✧ Relates the arrival of the Banū Ḥanīfah delegation with Musaylimah the liar, his false prophetic claims and rhymed sayings, the Prophet's ﷺ reply, and the appointment of agents over subdued lands.
✧ Provides a detailed account of the Prophet's ﷺ sole post-Hijrah pilgrimage in year ten, covering his journey, rites, sermons, special rulings, and return to Madinah.
✧ Covers the dispatch of Usāmah b. Zayd ؓ to al-Balqāʾ, the Prophet's ﷺ illness and death, and the subsequent mission of the army under Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq ؓ.
✧ Details the Prophet's ﷺ messengers and letters to various rulers, including the Negus, Caesar, Chosroes, and al-Muqawqis, and the outcomes of these correspondences.
✧ Summarizes the Prophet's ﷺ expeditions and raiding parties, their numbers, major battles, and selected accounts of specific missions led by his Companions.
✧ Describes the final illness of the Prophet ﷺ, his death, the events surrounding his passing, the grief of the Companions, and Abū Bakr's ؓ address to the community.
✧ Relates the gathering at the portico of Banū Sāʿidah where the Anṣār convened to choose a successor, leading to the pledge of allegiance to Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq ؓ as caliph.
✧ Details the washing, shrouding, prayer, and burial of the Prophet ﷺ, including the Companions' disagreements and the selection of his burial place.
✧ Lists the wives of the Prophet ﷺ and provides accounts of his marriages to each, along with their backgrounds and circumstances.
✧ Presents the history of the Rightly Guided Caliphate under Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq, ʿUmar b. al-Khaṭṭāb, ʿUthmān b. ʿAffān, and ʿAlī b. Abī Ṭālib, ؓ, covering their reigns and major events.
✧ Covers events in the caliphate of Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq from the pledge of allegiance through the Wars of Apostasy and conquests in Iraq until his death.
✧ Covers the caliphate of ʿUmar b. al-Khaṭṭāb from year 13 AH, including the conquest of Damascus, the Battle of al-Qādisiyya, and administrative developments until his death in 23 AH.
✧ Covers the caliphate of ʿUthmān b. ʿAffān from year 24 AH through the events of year 35 AH, including his merits and virtues.
✧ Covers the caliphate of ʿAlī b. Abī Ṭālib from year 35 AH, including the battles of the Camel and Ṣiffīn, and the caliphate of al-Ḥasan b. ʿAlī.
✧ Surveys the Umayyad caliphate from the reign of Muʿāwiyah b. Abī Sufyān through the caliphate of ʿUmar b. ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz up to the year 130 AH.
✧ Covers the caliphate of Muʿāwiyah b. Abī Sufyān from year 41 AH until his death in 60 AH, including a biography and account of his rule.
✧ Covers events of the year 61 AH, particularly the killing of al-Ḥusayn b. ʿAlī.
✧ Covers events of the year 62 AH, including the delegation of the people of al-Madīnah to Yazīd, the second governorship of ʿUqbah b. Nāfiʿ over Ifrīqiyah, and the revolt of Kusaylah.
✧ The Battle of al-Ḥarrah, notable deaths, and the controversial aftermath of Yazīd b. Muʿāwiyah's sack of Medina are surveyed.
✧ The Syrian march on Mecca, Yazīd's death and biography, Ibn al-Zubayr's caliphate, Kharijite revolts, and notable deaths are treated.
✧ The Tawwābūn's doomed expedition against Ibn Ziyād, Marwān's accession and death, ʿAbd al-Malik's caliphate, and other events are covered.
✧ Al-Mukhtār's rise in Kufa, his vengeance against al-Ḥusayn's killers, and the military and political events of the year are detailed.
✧ Ibn al-Ashtar's victory over Ibn Ziyād, Muṣʿab's conquest of Kufa, the killing of al-Mukhtār, and notable deaths are recounted.
✧ The Kharijite wars, the death of Ibn ʿAbbās, and the romantic tragedy of Qays b. Dharīḥ and Lubnā are covered.
✧ ʿAbd al-Malik's killing of ʿAmr b. Saʿīd, the Jarājima rebellion, and the lives of al-Aḥnaf and Abū al-Aswad are presented.
✧ The Qays–Taghlib wars, the rebellion and killing of Khālid b. Usayd, the plague in Egypt, and the story of Majnūn Laylā are covered.
✧ It recounts the killing of Muṣʿab b. al-Zubayr by ʿAbd al-Malik b. Marwān, his biography, the pledge of allegiance of Iraqis to ʿAbd al-Malik, and notable deaths.

✧ It covers battles of al-Muhallab with the Azāriqah, the emergence of Abū Fudayk, al-Ḥajjāj's dispatch against Ibn al-Zubayr, the killing of ʿAbd Allāh b. Khāzim, and deaths of al-Aḥnaf b. Qays and others.
✧ It provides a detailed biography of ʿAbd Allāh b. al-Zubayr and the circumstances of his killing.
✧ It covers al-Ḥajjāj's governorship of Madinah, his branding of Companions, demolition of the Kaʿbah structure, al-Muhallab's appointment against the Azāriqah, and the devastation of Ifrīqiyah.
✧ It relates al-Ḥajjāj's appointment over Iraq, his harsh sermon and killing of ʿUmayr b. Ḍābiʾ, the Basran uprising, battles with the Azāriqah, and the emergence of Ṣāliḥ b. Musarriḥ and Shabīb.
✧ It describes the rise of Ṣāliḥ b. Musarriḥ and Shabīb b. Yazīd against Muḥammad b. Marwān, their battles, Shabīb's entry into al-Kūfah, and the first minting of dirhams and dinars by ʿAbd al-Malik.
✧ It narrates Shabīb's battles against ʿAttāb b. Warqāʾ and Zuhrah b. Ḥawiyyah, his second entry into al-Kūfah, his eventual killing and drowning, and the wars of al-Muhallab with the Azāriqah.

✧ It covers the conquest of Irqiliyya, Mūsā b. Nuṣayr's appointment to the Maghrib, the dismissal of Umayyah b. ʿAbd Allāh from Khurāsān, al-Ḥajjāj's completion of Wāsiṭ, and deaths of Jābir b. ʿAbd Allāh and Shurayḥ.
✧ Covers the plague of Syria, ʿUbayd Allāh b. Abī Bakrah’s campaign against Ratbīl, and the killing of the false prophet al-Ḥārith b. Saʿīd.
✧ Reports the sweeping flood at Makkah, al-Muhallab’s expedition across the Balkh river, and al-Ḥajjāj’s campaign against Ratbīl.
✧ Relates the conquest of Qāliqalā, the killing of Baḥīr b. Warqāʾ, the Daylamite raid on Qazwīn, and Ibn al-Ashʿath’s rebellion.
✧ Details the dismissal of Abān b. ʿUthmān, the battles of al-Zāwiyah and Dayr al-Jamājim, and the death of al-Muhallab b. Abī Ṣufrah.
✧ Narrates the defeat of Ibn al-Ashʿath at Dayr al-Jamājim, al-Ḥajjāj’s execution of prisoners, and the building of Wāsiṭ.
✧ Mentions the conquest of al-Maṣṣīṣah, the killing of Ibn al-Ashʿath’s companions, the death of Ibn al-Ashʿath himself, and the capture of the fortress of Nīzak.
✧ Describes al-Ḥajjāj’s dismissal of Yazīd b. al-Muhallab, the killing of Mūsā b. ʿAbd Allāh b. Khāzim, and ʿAbd al-Malik’s attempt to remove his brother ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz.
✧ Reports Qutaybah b. Muslim’s campaigns, the Plague of the Maidens, Maslamah’s raid on Byzantium, and the death of Caliph ʿAbd al-Malik.
✧ Covers ʿUmar b. ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz's governorship of Madinah, Maslamah's Byzantine raid, Qutaybah's campaigns against the Turks including Baykand, and the deaths of several Companions and notables.
✧ Describes the conquest of Tyana, the expansion of the Prophet's Mosque, Qutaybah's victory over Kūrmaghānūn, and the construction of the Mosque of Damascus along with deaths of notable Companions.
✧ Includes Byzantine raids, Qutaybah's campaigns in Transoxiana, the conquest of Sind, Mūsā b. Nuṣayr's appointment over Ifrīqiyah, and the beginning of the Abbasid call.

✧ Details Maslamah's Byzantine campaign, Qutaybah's conquest of Bukhārā and dealings with Ṭarkhūn, the flight of Yazīd b. al-Muhallab from al-Ḥajjāj's prison, and deaths of notables like Anas b. Mālik.

✧ Records Maslamah's campaigns, Khālid al-Qasrī's governorship of Makkah, Mūsā b. Nuṣayr's Maghrib raids, Qutaybah's defeat of Nīzak, the conquest of Shūmān, Kishsh and Nasaf, and al-Walīd's pilgrimage.
✧ Covers Maslamah's Byzantine raids, the conquest of al-Andalus by Ṭāriq b. Ziyād and Mūsā b. Nuṣayr, Qutaybah's foray into Sijistān, the expedition to Sardinia, and deaths including Anas b. Mālik.

✧ Includes Byzantine campaigns by Maslamah and al-ʿAbbās, the flogging of Khubayb b. ʿAbd Allāh, Qutaybah's peace with Khwārizm Shāh, the conquest of Samarqand, and the dismissal of ʿUmar b. ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz.

✧ Describes raids into Byzantine territory, Qutaybah's campaigns in al-Shāsh and Farghānah, the killing of Saʿīd b. Jubayr, the deaths of major jurists, and the life of ʿAlī b. al-Ḥusayn Zayn al-ʿĀbidīn.

✧ Relates Ibn Būyah's capture of Shīrāz, seizure of Kirmān by Naṣr b. Aḥmad, deposition and blinding of al-Qāhir, caliphate of al-Rāḍī, death of the Fāṭimid al-Mahdī, Mardāwīj's seizure of al-Ahwāz, killing of Hārūn b. Gharīb, and execution of al-Shalmaghānī.

✧ Covers the killing of Mardāwīj and its aftermath, Washmagīr's consolidation, arrest of the sons of Yāqūt, rise of the Barīdīs, Ḥanbalī fitnah in Baghdad, killing of Abū al-ʿAlāʾ b. Ḥamdān, Ibn Muqlah's march to Mosul, and deaths of notables.

✧ Describes the arrest of Ibn Muqlah, killing of Yāqūt, Ibn Rāʾiq's seizure of affairs and fragmentation of the provinces, Muʿizz al-Dawlah's campaign in Kirmān, Mākān's seizure of Jurjān, and deaths of notables.

✧ Narrates estrangement and war between Ibn Rāʾiq and al-Barīdī, Bujkam's seizure of al-Ahwāz, the fragmentation of provinces, Sicilian revolt against the Fāṭimids, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Nāṣir's assumption of the caliphal title, and deaths of notables.
✧ Covers Muʿizz al-Dawlah's seizure of al-Ahwāz, the mutilation of Ibn Muqlah, Bujkam's takeover of Baghdad, war and peace with al-Barīdī, and other events of 326 AH.
✧ Relates al-Rāḍī and Bujkam's campaign to Mosul, the vizierates of al-Barīdī and Ibn Shīrzād, Bālubā's rebellion, and Abū ʿAlī's appointment in Khurasan.
✧ Describes Abū ʿAlī's conquest of Jurjān, Rukn al-Dawlah's campaigns, Bujkam's seizure of Wāsiṭ, Ibn Rāʾiq's acquisition of Syria, and other events of 328 AH.
✧ Narrates the death of al-Rāḍī, the accession of al-Muttaqī, the killing of Mākān b. Kālī, Bujkam's death, and the Barīdīs' brief control of Baghdad.
✧ Describes al-Barīdī's vizierate, Ibn Rāʾiq's killing, al-Muttaqī's refuge in Mosul, and the Barīdīs' oppressive rule in Baghdad.
✧ Recounts Nāṣir al-Dawlah's capture of ʿAdl al-Bujkamī, Sayf al-Dawlah's conflicts in Iraq, the accession of Nūḥ b. Naṣr, and other events of 331 AH.
✧ Covers al-Muttaqī's journey to Mosul, Muʿizz al-Dawlah's advance, the Barīdīs' fratricide, the Rūs' sack of Bardhaʿa, and other events of 332 AH.
✧ Relates al-Muttaqī's blinding and deposition, the accession of al-Mustakfī, and the rise and fall of the Khārijite rebel Abū Yazīd in Ifrīqiya.

✧ Covers Tūzūn's death, Ibn Shīrzād's command, Muʿizz al-Dawlah's seizure of Baghdād, the deposition of al-Mustakfī, accession of al-Muṭīʿ, war between Nāṣir al-Dawlah and Muʿizz al-Dawlah, deaths of al-Qāʾim and al-Ikhshīd, and other events of 334 AH.

✧ Events of 335 AH: peace between Muʿizz al-Dawlah and Nāṣir al-Dawlah, war involving Tikīn, Rukn al-Dawlah's seizure of al-Rayy, dispute with al-Barīdī, a prisoner exchange with Byzantium, and obituaries of notables.

✧ Events of 336 AH: Muʿizz al-Dawlah's seizure of al-Baṣrah, opposition of Muḥammad b. ʿAbd al-Razzāq in Ṭūs, governorship of al-Ḥasan b. ʿAlī in Sicily, rebellion of Jumān at al-Raḥbah, Rukn al-Dawlah's taking of Ṭabaristān and Jurjān, and notable deaths.

✧ Events of 337 AH: Muʿizz al-Dawlah's taking of Mosul, the Khurāsān army's march to Jurjān, al-Marzubān's march to al-Rayy, Sayf al-Dawlah's raid into Byzantine lands, arrest of Asfahdūst, and obituaries.
✧ Events of 338 AH: the affair of ʿImrān b. Shāhīn, death of al-Mustakfī, sectarian conflict in Baghdād, death of ʿImād al-Dawlah b. Buwayh, and obituaries of notables.

✧ Events of 339 AH: death of al-Ṣaymarī and vizierate of al-Muhallabī, Sayf al-Dawlah's Byzantine raid, Qarmaṭī return of the Black Stone, Khurāsānī march to al-Rayy, rout of Muʿizz al-Dawlah's armies by ʿImrān b. Shāhīn, and obituaries.

✧ Events of 340 AH: deaths of Manṣūr b. Qarātakīn and Abū al-Muẓaffar b. Muḥtāj, Abū ʿAlī's return to Khurāsān, war in Sicily between Muslims and Byzantines, sectarian fitnah in Ramaḍān, and obituaries.

✧ Events of 341 AH: siege of al-Baṣrah by Yūsuf b. Wajīh, Byzantine capture of Surūj, death of al-Manṣūr al-ʿAlawī and reign of al-Muʿizz, Rukn al-Dawlah's campaign in Ṭabaristān and Jurjān, birth of Fakhr al-Dawlah, and obituaries.
✧ Daysam b. Ibrahim's flight from Adharbayjan to Baghdad and his later blinding are recounted, together with al-Marzuban's escape from Sumayram and his restoration of his territories.
✧ Abu ʿAli b. Muhtaj seeks refuge with Rukn al-Dawla, aids in defeating Bakr b. Malik, but flees Khurasan after Nuh's death; Sayf al-Dawla raids Byzantium, and notable deaths are recorded.
✧ Muʿizz al-Dawla's severe illness and Ibn Shahin's revolt, the Khurasani campaign against al-Rayy and Isbahan, epidemics, and deaths of prominent scholars and officials are detailed.
✧ Ruzbahan's rebellion against Muʿizz al-Dawla is crushed despite initial success, Sayf al-Dawla raids Byzantine lands, and notable deaths including Abu ʿUmar Ghulam Thaʿlab are recorded.
✧ Al-Marzuban dies and his brother Wahsudhan contends with his nephews; Muʿizz al-Dawla marches against Nasir al-Dawla but turns back; earthquakes, plagues, and deaths of scholars occur.
✧ Muʿizz al-Dawla captures Mosul but withdraws after supplies are cut, Jawhar's Maghrib campaign reaches the Atlantic and captures Sijilmasa and Fas, and notable deaths are listed.

✧ Peace between Sayf al-Dawla and Muʿizz al-Dawla is concluded, Byzantines raid Tarsus and al-Ruha, famine and sectarian strife occur, and many notable deaths including scholars and Sufis are recorded.
✧ Al-Mustajir billah's abortive bid for power in Adharbayjan is suppressed, Wahsudhan treacherously kills his nephews, Sayf al-Dawla suffers losses in his Byzantine raid, and many deaths are noted.
✧ Events of 350 AH include Muʿizz al-Dawla's construction of his Baghdād residence, Byzantine raids, the deaths of several rulers, and biographies of notable scholars.

✧ Events of 351 AH include the Byzantine capture of ʿAyn Zarbah and Aleppo, Rukn al-Dawla's seizure of Ṭabaristān and Jurjān, sectarian inscriptions in Baghdād, and the conquest of Ṭabarmīn in Sicily.
✧ Events of 352 AH include the rebellion of Ḥarrān, the death of the vizier al-Muhallabī, raids against Byzantium, and ʿĀshūrāʾ commemorations in Baghdād.
✧ Events of 353 AH include the rebellion of Najā, Byzantine sieges of al-Maṣṣīṣah and Ṭarsūs, Muʿizz al-Dawla's campaign in al-Mawṣil, and the Battle of the Strait in Sicily.
✧ Events of 354 AH include the Byzantine conquest of al-Maṣṣīṣah and Ṭarsūs, the revolt of Antioch against Sayf al-Dawlah, the rebellion in Sijistān, and the death of al-Mutanabbī.
✧ Events of 355 AH include Muʿizz al-Dawla's campaign in ʿUmān, conflicts in Adharbayjān, Khurāsānī ghāzīs at al-Rayy, Byzantine incursions, and the death of Ibn al-Jiʿābī.
✧ Events of 356 AH include the death of Muʿizz al-Dawla, the misrule of his successor Bakhtiyār, the Khurāsānī expedition against al-Rayy, and the arrest of Nāṣir al-Dawlah.
✧ Events of 357 AH include the revolt of Ḥubshī against Bakhtiyār, the affair of Muḥammad b. al-Mustakfī, ʿAḍud al-Dawla's conquest of Kirmān, and the killing of Abū Firās.
✧ Jawhar's Fāṭimid conquest of Egypt, capture of Damascus, Ḥamdānid family strife, Byzantine raids, Qarghawayh's seizure of Aleppo, and notable obituaries.
✧ Byzantine captures of Antioch, Aleppo, and Malazkard, Ibn al-ʿAmīd's campaign against Ḥasanūyah, the murder of Emperor Nikephoros, and Abū Taghlib's takeover of Ḥarrān.
✧ Qarmaṭī seizure of Damascus and defeat of Jaʿfar b. Falāḥ, killing of Muḥammad b. al-Ḥusayn al-Zanātī, ʿAḍud al-Dawlah's suppression of Kirmān rebels, and prominent deaths including al-Ṭabarānī.
✧ Byzantine devastation of al-Jazīrah, Baghdad sectarian strife, al-Muʿizz's departure from Ifrīqiya to Egypt, Yūsuf Bulukkīn's background, and Sāmānid–Būyid peace.
✧ Byzantine incursions and their defeat at Mayyāfāriqīn, the burning of al-Karkh, the vizierate of Ibn Baqiyya, and al-Muʿizz's entry into Egypt.
✧ Bakhtiyār's failed campaign against Abū Taghlib, the Turk–Daylam discord and Subuktikīn's coup, the deposition of al-Muṭīʿ and accession of al-Ṭāʾiʿ, and al-Muʿizz's defeats of the Qarmaṭīs.
✧ ʿAḍud al-Dawlah's seizure of Iraq and arrest of Bakhtiyār, Kirmān rebellion suppressed, al-Fatikīn's governorship of Damascus and eventual capture, and various Baghdad events.
✧ Death of al-Muʿizz and accession of al-ʿAzīz, Yūsuf Bulukkīn's western campaigns, Sicilian raids, Rukn al-Dawlah's division of kingdoms, and prominent obituaries including Ibn ʿAdī.

✧ Covers the death of Rukn al-Dawlah and succession of ʿAḍud al-Dawlah, including his campaign against Bakhtiyār in Iraq, the Samanid succession, deaths of scholars and rulers, the rise of Subuktigīn in Ghaznah, and events in al-Andalus.
✧ Describes ʿAḍud al-Dawlah’s seizure of Iraq, the killing of Bakhtiyār, conquest of the Ḥamdānid lands, and various events including floods, earthquakes, and the death of notables.
✧ Narrates the conquest of Mayyāfāriqīn and Diyār Bakr by ʿAḍud al-Dawlah, Qassām’s governorship of Damascus, earthquakes, the khuṭbah for ʿAḍud al-Dawlah, and obituaries of scholars.

✧ Relates the killing of Abū Taghlib b. Ḥamdān, wars with the Baṭīḥah and Banū Shaybān, the Byzantine rebel Ward’s arrival, ʿAḍud al-Dawlah’s reconstruction of Baghdādh, and his seizure of Fakhr al-Dawlah’s lands.

✧ Includes Muʾayyid al-Dawlah’s grant of Hamadhān, the killing of Ḥasanūyah’s sons except Badr, ʿAḍud al-Dawlah’s capture of Sandah, the defeat of Ibn Jarrāḥ by Egyptian forces, and various events including the wedding of ʿAḍud al-Dawlah’s daughter to the caliph.

✧ Records the dismissal of Ibn Sīmjūr from Khurāsān, ʿAḍud al-Dawlah’s seizure of Jurjān, the attempted reconquest by Ḥusām al-Dawlah and Qābūs, the death of the Sicilian amīr Abū al-Qāsim in battle, and several fires and arrests in Baghdādh.

✧ Describes Bakjūr’s governorship of Damascus, the death of ʿAḍud al-Dawlah and accession of Ṣamṣām al-Dawlah, the killing of al-Ḥusayn b. ʿImrān b. Shāhīn, Ibn Sīmjūr’s return to Khurāsān, and obituaries.

✧ Reports the death of Muʾayyid al-Dawlah and restoration of Fakhr al-Dawlah, the dismissal of Abū al-ʿAbbās from Khurāsān, the killing of Abū al-Faraj in al-Baṭīḥah, the rise of Muḥammad b. Ghānim, and Ṣinhāja military actions in al-Andalus.
✧ Covers the defeat of Bādh the Kurd by Zayyār and the Daylamites, the peace settlement over Diyār Bakr, various political appointments and events, and obituaries of notable scholars and figures.

✧ Describes the strife in Baghdad over Ṣamṣām al-Dawlah, Qarāmiṭa actions in al-Kūfah, the release of Ward the Byzantine and Rus conversion, Sharaf al-Dawlah taking al-Ahwāz, al-Manṣūr's defeat in Fās, and obituaries of scholars.
✧ Narrates Sharaf al-Dawlah's seizure of Iraq, the Turkish-Daylamite conflict, the governorship of Muhadhdhab al-Dawlah over al-Baṭīḥah, and deaths of numerous scholars.
✧ Details the war between Badr b. Ḥasanūyah and Sharaf al-Dawlah's army, al-Manṣūr's campaign against Kutāmah, Bādh's renewed fighting in al-Mawṣil, and obituaries of notables.
✧ Covers the arrests of Shukr and Bakjūr, al-Aṣfar's victory over the Qarāmiṭa, various events in Iraq and Iran, and obituaries of prominent scholars.

✧ Narrates the blinding of Ṣamṣām al-Dawlah, the death of Sharaf al-Dawlah, the journey of his son to Fārs, strife between Turks and Daylamites, Fakhr al-Dawlah's march to Iraq, and the return of the Banū Ḥamdān to al-Mawṣil.
✧ Covers the killing of Bādh and the rise of the Banū Marwān, the rule of al-Musayyab's family over al-Mawṣil, Bahāʾ al-Dawlah's campaign to al-Ahwāz, riots in Baghdad, and obituaries of notables.
✧ Details the arrest and deposition of al-Ṭāʾiʿ, the accession of al-Qādir bi-Allāh, events in Egypt and Syria, and obituaries of notables.
✧ In 382 AH the Daylam's return to al-Mawṣil, al-Ṭāʾiʿ's handover to al-Qādir, several events in Baghdad and elsewhere, and deaths of notable scholars are recounted.
✧ In 383 AH the emergence of Bakhtiyār's sons, Ṣamṣām al-Dawlah's seizure of Khūzistān, the Turk's possession of Bukhārā, Nūḥ's return, and various events and deaths are covered.
✧ In 384 AH Maḥmūd b. Subuktikīn's appointment over Khurāsān, Bahāʾ al-Dawlah's taking of al-Ahwāz, several events, and deaths of notables are recounted.
✧ In 385 AH Abū ʿAlī's return to Khurāsān, his capture and death, al-Ṣāḥib b. ʿAbbād's death, Ṣamṣām al-Dawlah's slaughter of Turks, and deaths of several notables are covered.
✧ In 386 AH al-ʿAzīz's death and al-Ḥākim's succession, Ṣamṣām al-Dawlah's seizure of al-Baṣrah, al-Muqallid's governorship of al-Mawṣil, and Bādīs's succession in Ifrīqiya are recounted.
✧ In 387 AH Nūḥ b. Manṣūr's death, Subuktikīn's death and Ismāʿīl's brief reign, Maḥmūd's seizure of power, and deaths of prominent scholars are covered.
✧ In 388 AH Abū al-Qāsim al-Sīmjūrī's return to Naysābūr, Maḥmūd b. Subuktikīn's seizure of Naysābūr, Qābūs's return to Jurjān, and Ṣamṣām al-Dawlah's killing are recounted.
✧ In 389 AH Manṣūr b. Nūḥ's seizure and blinding, Maḥmūd's seizure of Khurāsān, the extinction of the Sāmānid dynasty, and Bahāʾ al-Dawlah's possession of Fāris and Khūzistān are covered.

✧ It covers the escape and campaigns of the Sāmānid al-Muntaṣir, Maḥmūd of Ghazna's siege of Sijistān, the killing of Ibn Bakhtiyār, the arrest of al-Muwaffaq, and obituaries of notable scholars and officials.
✧ It recounts the killing of al-Muqallid al-ʿUqaylī, the accession of his son Qirwāsh, al-Qādir's pledge of allegiance to his son al-Ghālib bi-llāh, and deaths of notable figures.
✧ It describes Maḥmūd of Ghazna's campaigns in India, wars between Qirwāsh and the Būyid army in Iraq, civil strife and fiscal disturbances in Baghdad, and obituaries of scholars and poets.
✧ It covers Maḥmūd of Ghazna's conquest of Sijistān, the death of al-Manṣūr b. Abī ʿĀmir in al-Andalus, Fulfūl's siege of Qābis, and deaths of scholars and poets.
✧ It narrates Abū al-ʿAbbās b. Wāṣil's seizure of al-Baṭīḥah, appointments of the sharīf al-Raḍī and others in Iraq, and obituaries of notable figures.
✧ It recounts the restoration of Muhadhdhab al-Dawla to al-Baṭīḥa, Maḥmūd's raid on Bahāṭiyah in India, famine in Ifrīqiyah, and deaths of ḥadīth scholars and lexicographers.
✧ It describes Maḥmūd of Ghazna's campaigns against Multan and the fortress of Kawākīr, Īlak Khān's invasion of Khurāsān, and a defeat of the Būyid army by Kurds.
✧ It recounts Maḥmūd's defeat of Īlak Khān and his Indian raid, the siege of Baghdad, the killing of Abū al-ʿAbbās b. Wāṣil, and the revolt of Abū Rakwah against al-Ḥākim.
✧ Yamīn al-Dawla's expedition against Bahīm Nughur, the seizure of its idol treasures, and Abū Jaʿfar b. Kākawayh's restoration in Iṣfahān.
✧ The rise of Ṣāliḥ b. Mirdās at al-Raḥbah through betraying Ibn Maḥkān, and various events including a meteor fall and the weakening of Umayyad authority in al-Andalus.

✧ Yamīn al-Dawla's campaign ending in a peace treaty, the conflict between Badr b. Ḥasanawayh and his son Hilāl, al-Muʾayyad's restoration in al-Andalus, and al-Ḥākim's opening of Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq's house.
✧ Yamīn al-Dawla's campaigns against the Ghūrīs and infidels, Aylak Khān's aborted war with his brother, and Qirwāsh's establishment of the Egyptian daʿwah.
✧ Yamīn al-Dawla's seizure of Quṣdār, Ṣāliḥ b. Mirdās's capture and later possession of Aleppo, and the killing of a group from Khafājah.
✧ The killing of Qābūs b. Washmakīr, the accession of Tughān Khān after Aylak Khān's death, Sulṭān al-Dawlah's succession to Bahāʾ al-Dawlah, and Sulaymān b. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān's rule in al-Andalus.
✧ Yamīn al-Dawlah's conquest of Nārdīn, Khafājah's plundering of the sawād of al-Kūfah, and Ṭāhir b. Hilāl's seizure of Shahrazūr.
✧ Yamīn al-Dawlah's raid on Tānīshar, the killing of Badr b. Ḥasanawayh and subsequent death of his son Hilāl, ʿAlī b. Mazyad's war with Banū Dubays, and Shams al-Dawla's occupation of al-Rayy.
✧ It covers the civil war in Ifrīqiya between Bādīs and his uncle Ḥammād, Bādīs's death and the accession of his young son al-Muʿizz, Maḥmūd's Indian expeditions, and the killing of Fakhr al-Mulk.

✧ It reports Mahmud of Ghazna's conquests of Khwarazm, Qishmir, and Qannuj, the rise of Ibn Fuladh, the Alid dynasty in al-Andalus, and lists notable deaths such as Abu Hamid al-Isfarayini and al-Sharif al-Radi.
✧ It details the Turkish incursions from China, the succession of the Qarakhanid khans, the deaths of Muhadhdhib al-Dawla and Ali b. Mazyad, and conflicts between Sunnis and Shi'ites in Baghdad.
✧ It covers Ibn Sahlan's governorship of Iraq, Mahmud of Ghazni's campaigns in India, and the deaths of scholars such as the hadith master Abd al-Ghani al-Azdi.
✧ It narrates Mahmud of Ghazni's conquest of fortresses in India and the submission of thousands of idolaters, along with the deaths of several prominent hadith transmitters.
✧ It focuses on the disappearance and presumed murder of the Fatimid caliph al-Hakim, the accession of his son al-Zahir, and the power struggles among the Buyids in Iraq.
✧ It describes the transfer of power in Iraq to Musharrif al-Dawla, the death of the vizier Abu Ghalib, and the deaths of notable calligrapher Ibn al-Bawwab and several scholars.
✧ It relates the peace between Buyid rivals Sultan al-Dawla and Musharrif al-Dawla, the killing of the Ifriqiyan vizier, and the breaking of the Black Stone by an Egyptian pilgrim.
✧ Covers ʿAlāʾ al-Dawlah's seizure of Hamadhān, the vizierate of Abū al-Qāsim al-Maghribī, a fortress conquest in India, caliphal events, and deaths of notables.
✧ Covers the breach between Musharrif al-Dawla and the Turks, strife in Kufa, the death of Sulṭān al-Dawlah and succession of Abū Kālījār, Kharijite revolt, and deaths of notables.
✧ Covers Maḥmūd's conquest of Sūmanāt, the death of Musharrif al-Dawla and accession of Jalāl al-Dawla, Naṣr al-Dawla's seizure of al-Ruhā, Sicilian fleet disaster, and deaths of notables.
✧ Covers wars involving ʿAlāʾ al-Dawlah, Qirwāsh, and Khafāja, peace in Ifrīqiya, natural phenomena, and deaths of notables.
✧ Covers ʿAlāʾ al-Dawlah's war with Isbahbadh, rebellion in al-Baṭīḥah, reconciliation between Abū Kālījār and his uncle, Jalāl al-Dawla's entry into Baghdad, and deaths of notables.
✧ Covers Badrān's war with Naṣr al-Dawlah, Turkish disturbance in Baghdad, Abū Kālījār's seizure of al-Baṣrah, and deaths of notables.
✧ Covers Maḥmūd's seizure of al-Rayy and al-Jabal, Ibrāhīm b. al-Marzubān's actions, Abū Kālījār's seizure of Wāsiṭ, Ghuzz affairs, and deaths of notables.
✧ Covers Masʿūd's seizure of Hamadhān, Maḥmūd's death and succession, wars between various rulers, the Byzantine campaign, and deaths of notables.
✧ Events of 422 AH include Masʿūd b. Maḥmūd's seizures of Tīz, Mukrān, and Kirmān, the Byzantine capture of al-Ruhāʾ, the death of al-Qādir and succession of al-Qāʾim, and strife in Baghdad.
✧ In 423 AH the troops expelled Jalāl al-Dawlah from Baghdad, ʿAlāʾ al-Dawla was defeated by Masʿūd's army, plague and famine struck many lands, and notable figures died.
✧ In 424 AH Masʿūd returned to Ghazna, subdued the lord of Sāwah, Jalāl al-Dawlah took and lost al-Baṣrah, and the ʿayyārūn spread disorder in Baghdad.
✧ In 425 AH Masʿūd conquered Sarastī and other Indian fortresses, strife broke out in Naysābūr and between the Mazyadid brothers, and the Byzantines seized Birkawī.
✧ In 426 AH the caliphate and sultanate in Baghdad fell into disorder, Aḥmad Yanāltikīn rebelled and was killed, Masʿūd took Jurjān and Ṭabaristān, and Ibn Waththāb raided Ibn Marwān's land.
✧ In 427 AH troops rose against Jalāl al-Dawlah, ʿAlāʾ al-Dawla was defeated by Abū Sahl al-Ḥamdūnī, al-Ẓāhir died and al-Mustanṣir succeeded as Fatimid caliph, and several notables died.
✧ In 428 AH Bārasṭughān rebelled and was killed by Jalāl al-Dawlah, peace and marriage alliance was made with Abū Kālījār, Ibn Sīnā died, and the ʿayyārūn rose in Baghdad.
✧ In 429 AH the Abkhazians besieged Tiflis and retreated before the Ghuzz, Tughrulbak entered Naysābūr, and Jalāl al-Dawlah was addressed as King of Kings.

✧ Covers King Masʿūd's campaign expelling the Saljūq Turks from Khurasan, Abū al-Shawk's conquest of Khūlanjān, the Abbasid khuṭbah in Ḥarrān and al-Raqqah, natural phenomena and administrative changes in Baghdad, and deaths of notables.

✧ Records Masʿūd's capture of a fortress from the Ghuzz, Abū Kālījār's seizure of al-Baṣrah, upheaval in ʿUmān, war between Abū al-Shawk and his uncle Muhalhil, Turkish riots in Baghdad, and obituaries of prominent figures.

✧ Describes the rise of the Seljuq state under Ṭughrul-Bek and Dāwūd, the arrest and killing of Sultan Masʿūd, Mawdūd's succession, discord between Jalāl al-Dawlah and Qirwāsh, Abū al-Shawk's conquest of Daqūqā, and a Muslim victory over the Byzantines.
✧ Reports the death of ʿAlāʾ al-Dawlah, Ṭughrul-Bek's conquest of Jurjān and Ṭabaristān, Byzantine court intrigues, the downfall of al-Dizbarī in Syria, and the promulgation of the Qādirī creed.
✧ Relates Ṭughrul-Bek's capture of Khwārazm and al-Rayy, Ibrāhīm Yināl's operations in al-Jabal, fighting over Kirmān, al-Qāʾim's estrangement from Jalāl al-Dawlah, and Sukayn's uprising in Egypt.

✧ Covers the year 558 AH, including the vizierates of Shāwar and al-Ḍirghām in Egypt, the death of ʿAbd al-Muʾmin and succession of Yūsuf, Nūr al-Dīn's defeat at al-Buqayʿa, the expulsion of Banū Asad from Iraq, and deaths of notables.

✧ Relates the events of 559 AH, chiefly Shīrkūh's first expedition to Egypt and his return, Nūr al-Dīn's conquests of Ḥārim and Bāniyās, the death of the vizier Jamāl al-Dīn, and various regional conflicts and obituaries.

✧ Describes the year 560 AH, including the death of the Shāh of Māzandarān, al-Muʾayyad's seizure of Herat, the war between Qalj Arsilān and Ibn Dānishmand, and the death and virtues of the vizier Ibn Hubayra.
✧ Covers 561 AH, including Nūr al-Dīn's conquest of al-Munayṭira, the killing of Khaṭalbers, the death of ʿAbd al-Qādir al-Jīlī, and other obituaries and miscellaneous events.
✧ Relates the year 562 AH, chiefly Shīrkūh's return to Egypt and victory at al-Bābayn, his taking of Alexandria, Nūr al-Dīn's raids in Frankish territory, and conflicts in Iraq and elsewhere.

✧ Describes 563 AH, including Zayn al-Dīn's departure from Mosul, the war between al-Bahlawān and the lord of Marāgha, the appointment of Ibn al-Baladī as vizier, and the deaths of al-Samʿānī and others.
✧ Covers the year 564 AH, highlighting Nūr al-Dīn's taking of Qalʿat Jaʿbar, Shīrkūh's conquest of Egypt and killing of Shāwar, the death of Shīrkūh, and Ṣalāḥ al-Dīn's accession to power.

✧ Relates the events of 565 AH, including the Frankish siege of Damietta, Nūr al-Dīn's siege of al-Karak, the great earthquake in Syria, the death of Quṭb al-Dīn Mawdūd, and various obituaries and occurrences.
✧ Covers the death of Caliph al-Mustanjid bi-Allāh, the accession of al-Mustaḍīʾ bi-Amr Allāh, Nūr al-Dīn's taking of Mosul, Ṣalāḥ al-Dīn's conquest of Aylah, and obituaries of notables in 566 AH.
✧ Covers the establishment of the Abbasid khuṭbah in Egypt ending the Fāṭimid dynasty, the death of al-ʿĀḍid, estrangement between Nūr al-Dīn and Ṣalāḥ al-Dīn, and other events of 567 AH.
✧ Covers the death of Khwārazmshāh Arslān and the succession struggles of Sulṭān Shāh and Tekish, the death of al-Muʾayyad and his son's accession, and other events in Khurāsān up to 568 AH.

✧ Covers Shams al-Dawla Tūrānshāh's conquest of Yemen including Zabīd and Aden, the killing of Egyptian conspirators against Ṣalāḥ al-Dīn, and the death and eulogies of Nūr al-Dīn Maḥmūd b. Zankī in 569 AH.

✧ Covers the defeat of the Sicilian fleet at Alexandria, the rebellion of al-Kanz in Upper Egypt, Ṣalāḥ al-Dīn's acquisition of Damascus, Ḥimṣ, and Ḥamāh, and the flight of Quṭb al-Dīn Qāymāz from Baghdad in 569 AH.
✧ Covers the defeat of Sayf al-Dīn's army by Ṣalāḥ al-Dīn near Ḥamāh, Ṣalāḥ al-Dīn's subsequent siege of Aleppo and peace agreement, the sedition in Makkah, and deaths of notables in 571 AH.
✧ Covers Ṣalāḥ al-Dīn's plundering of Ismāʿīlī territory, the siege of Masyāf, Muslim-Frankish engagements, the rebellion of the lord of Shahrazūr, and the plundering of al-Bandanījīn in 572 AH.
✧ Covers the defeat of Ṣalāḥ al-Dīn at al-Ramla, the Frankish siege of Ḥamāh, the killing of Kumushtakīn and siege of Ḥārim, and the assassination of the vizier Ibn Raʾīs al-Ruʾasāʾ in 573 AH.

✧ Franks raid and devastate villages around Ḥamāh, but the city's garrison routs them; Ibn al-Muqaddam rebels at Baʿlabakk, which Ṣalāḥ al-Dīn besieges and gives to his brother Shams al-Dawla after compensation.
✧ Ṣalāḥ al-Dīn's forces defeat Qilij Arslān's army after the latter besieges Raʿbān; the Franks' fortress at Bayt al-Aḥzān is destroyed; al-Mustaḍīʾ dies and al-Nāṣir succeeds him.
✧ Sayf al-Dīn Ghāzī of Mosul dies and is succeeded by his brother ʿIzz al-Dīn Masʿūd; Ṣalāḥ al-Dīn marches against Qilij Arslān and raids Ibn Līyūn's Armenian territory.
✧ Farrukhshāh raids Karak to thwart Prince Arnāṭ's planned attack on Medina; Ṣalāḥ al-Dīn sends armies to Yemen; al-Malik al-Ṣāliḥ dies and Aleppo passes to ʿIzz al-Dīn Masʿūd.

✧ Ṣalāḥ al-Dīn marches from Egypt to Syria, raids Frankish lands, captures a cave fortress, sends his brother Ṭughtikīn to Yemen, crosses the Euphrates to conquer Jazīrah territory, besieges Mosul, takes Sinjār, and defeats Franks at sea.
✧ Ṣalāḥ al-Dīn takes Āmid and gives it to Nūr al-Dīn Muḥammad, captures Tall Khālid and ʿAyn Tāb, wins engagements at sea and in Syria, acquires Aleppo, and takes Ḥārim.
✧ Mujāhid al-Dīn is released and the Persians defeated; Yūsuf b. ʿAbd al-Muʾmin dies and Yaʿqūb succeeds; Ṣalāḥ al-Dīn raids al-Karak; the veiled Ibn Ghāniya seizes Bijāya; the lord of Māridīn dies.

✧ Ṣalāḥ al-Dīn besieges Mosul again but departs after Shāh Arman's death; Nūr al-Dīn of Ḥiṣn dies; Ṣalāḥ al-Dīn captures Mayyāfāriqīn; peace is made with Mosul; Turkmen-Kurdish strife; Almohads defeat the veiled ones in Ifrīqiyah.

✧ The year 582 AH witnessed Ṣalāḥ al-Dīn's redistribution of provinces among his kin, internal Muslim and Frankish conflicts, Prince Arnāṭ's treacherous caravan raid, and predictions about a planetary conjunction.

✧ This year saw Ṣalāḥ al-Dīn's devastating defeat of the Franks at Ḥiṭṭīn, the conquest of Jerusalem, and the subjugation of most coastal and inland Frankish territories, along with notable deaths and eastern affairs.

✧ The year 584 AH chronicles Ṣalāḥ al-Dīn's final campaigns against remaining Frankish strongholds in Syria, including Ṣahyūn, al-Shughr, Barzayh, Darb Sāk, Baghrās, al-Karak, Ṣafad, and Kawkab, plus events in Egypt and the East.

✧ This year covers the prolonged Frankish siege of Acre, the arrival of Frankish reinforcements by sea, the death of Taqī al-Dīn, and various battles and minor engagements between Muslim and Frankish forces.

✧ In 586 AH the Franks' siege of Acre continued with the burning of their siege towers, the disastrous German crusade, and the fall of Acre, followed by the Franks' southward march and destructive engagements at Arsūf and elsewhere.
✧ The year 588 AH recounts the death of Saladin, the subsequent disputes among his heirs, and the campaigns of other regional rulers such as Atabeg ʿIzz al-Dīn and the lord of Khilāṭ.
✧ This year details the truce between Ṣalāḥ al-Dīn and the Franks, the king of England's activities, the return to Damascus, and the deaths of Qilij Arslān and other notables.
✧ The year 589 AH describes the death and burial of Saladin, his character and family, and the subsequent movements of al-ʿĀdil and other contemporary rulers such as Atabeg ʿIzz al-Dīn.

✧ Covers Shihāb al-Dīn al-Ghūrī's victory over the king of Banāras, the killing of Sultan Tughrul and Khwārizm Shāh's consolidation, the caliphal vizier's conquest of Khūzistān, al-ʿAzīz's siege of Damascus, and various deaths and events.

✧ Describes the caliphal vizier's campaigns in Persian lands, the Almohad victory at al-Zallāqah, the uprising of ʿAlī al-Mulaththam in Ifrīqiya, al-ʿAzīz's second failed siege of Damascus, and other events and obituaries.
✧ Relates Shihāb al-Dīn al-Ghūrī's Indian campaigns, al-ʿĀdil's seizure of Damascus from al-Afḍal, natural phenomena in Iraq and Arabia, and obituaries of scholars.
✧ Includes the failed mission of Abū al-Hayjāʾ al-Samīn in Hamadhān, Frankish capture of Beirut and siege of Tibnīn, the death of Sayf al-Islām in Yemen, and various events and obituaries.
✧ Chronicles the death of ʿImād al-Dīn Zangī and succession in Sinjār, Nūr al-Dīn's seizure of Naṣībīn, Ghūrid victories over the Khiṭā and conquest of Balkh, and other events and obituaries.
✧ Details the death of al-ʿAzīz and al-Afḍal's accession in Egypt, his failed siege of Damascus, the Almohad succession after Yaʿqūb, and various internal affairs and obituaries.
✧ Recounts al-ʿĀdil's takeover of Egypt, the death of Khwārizm Shāh Tukush and his son's accession, a severe famine in Egypt, and the deaths of notable scholars.
✧ Describes al-Ẓāhir's and al-Afḍal's unsuccessful siege of Damascus, Ghūrid advances in Khurāsān against Khwārizm Shāh, Rukn al-Dīn's conquests, and devastating earthquakes and famine.
✧ Covers Khwārazm Shāh Muḥammad's campaigns to recover Khurāsān and Herat from the Ghūrids, his peace negotiations, and the deaths of prominent scholars and officials.
✧ Describes al-ʿĀdil's siege of Mārdīn, the death of Ghiyāth al-Dīn al-Ghūrī, al-Ẓāhir's seizure of Qalʿat Najm, the Georgian capture of Duwīn, and other events.
✧ Details Khwārazm Shāh's second siege of Herat, Shihāb al-Dīn's defeat by the Khiṭā, the Frankish conquest of Constantinople, and notable deaths including ʿAbd al-Ghanī al-Maqdisī.
✧ Relates Kaykhusraw's restoration in Rūm, the siege of Khart Birt, seditions in Baghdad, Georgian raids, the Makkah-Madīnah war, and deaths of several scholars and poets.
✧ Covers the sedition in Herat, Shihāb al-Dīn's war against the Banū Kawkar and his assassination, Aldiz's seizure of Ghazna, and other regional conflicts.
✧ Describes the struggle for Ghazna among Aldiz, ʿAlāʾ al-Dīn, and Ghiyāth al-Dīn after Shihāb al-Dīn's death, along with ʿAbbās's seizure of Bāmiyān.
✧ Narrates Khwārazm Shāh's campaigns against the Khiṭā, his captivity and escape, and his eventual conquest of Herat and the Ghūrid territories.
✧ Records the Georgian sack of Arjīsh, the murder of Sanjar Shāh, and other events including an earthquake in Naysābūr.
✧ Al-ʿĀdil's seizure of al-Khābūr and Naṣībīn, his siege of Sinjār and peace settlement, followed by miscellaneous events and obituaries of prominent figures.
✧ The caliphal campaign against the rebellious mamlūk Sanjar in Khūzistān, the death and succession of Nūr al-Dīn Araslān Shāh, and other events and notable deaths.
✧ Mankilī's seizure of lands and Īdghamish's flight to Baghdad, along with earthquakes, the Ismāʿīlī conversion, pilgrim plunder at Minā, and obituaries of scholars.
✧ The arrival of Mankilī's son in Baghdad, followed by the suppression of Sāma al-Jabalī's revolt, the exile of Ibn Shukr, and obituaries of several scholars.
✧ The killing of Īdghamish by Mankalī's partisans, various events including the pilgrimage and Khwārazm Shāh's espionage, and obituaries of prominent figures.
✧ Khwārazm Shāh's conquest of Kirmān, Makrān, and al-Sind, along with the killing of Muʾayyad al-Mulk and other events of the year and notable deaths.
✧ The defeat and killing of Mankalī, the caliph's son's death, Khwārazm Shāh's acquisition of Ghaznah, Alduz's seizure of Lahore and subsequent death, and other events with obituaries.
✧ The death of al-Malik al-Ẓāhir of Aleppo and succession arrangements, various natural and urban events, and detailed obituaries of numerous scholars and poets.
✧ Covers Khwārazm Shāh ʿAlāʾ al-Dīn Muḥammad's conquest of al-Jabal, Atabeg Saʿd's conflict with his sons, and the Frankish siege and eventual Muslim recovery of Damietta.
✧ Recounts the death of al-Malik al-Qāhir, the ensuing succession struggles in Mosul, Kaykāʾūs's failed campaign against Aleppo, and the death of al-Malik al-ʿĀdil.
✧ Describes the accession of Kayqubād in Rūm, the murder of the lord of Sinjār, the defeat of the Banū Maʿrūf, and the first appearance of the Tatars under Chingiz Khan.
✧ Chronicles the devastation wrought by the Tatars as they overran Transoxiana, Khurāsān, Azerbaijan, and the Qipchaq steppe, including the fall of Bukhārā and Samarqand.
✧ Details the death of Qatāda, amir of Makkah, the murderous usurpation by his son al-Ḥasan, and the peace agreement that restored Damietta to the Muslims.
✧ Relates the Qifjāq migration into Azerbaijan, their betrayals of Shirwān Shāh and the Georgians, the Karaj plunder of Baylaqān, and Badr al-Dīn's capture of Shūsh.
✧ Tells of al-Malik al-Masʿūd Aqsīs's seizure of Makkah, the war between the lord of Surmārī and the Georgians, and the rebellion of Ghiyāth al-Dīn's maternal uncle.
✧ Describes a fresh Tatar raid on al-Rayy and Hamadhān, Ghiyāth al-Dīn's conquest of Fārs, Shihāb al-Dīn's revolt against al-Ashraf, and the failed siege of Mosul.
✧ In the year 622 AH, the Georgians besiege Ganjah but are repelled, Jalāl al-Dīn Khwārazm Shāh moves through Khūzistān and Iraq, and internal conflicts in Shirwān lead to a change of ruler.

✧ In the year 623 AH, the Caliph al-Ẓāhir dies and is succeeded by al-Mustanṣir bi'llāh, Jalāl al-Dīn defeats the Georgians and captures Tiflis, and various internal conflicts and natural phenomena are recorded.
✧ In the year 624 AH, the Georgians burn Tiflis, Jalāl al-Dīn campaigns against the Ismāʿīlīs and Tatars, and the death of Genghis Khān is recorded among other notable events.
✧ In the year 625 AH, internal discord among the Khwārazmians, wars with the Tatars, Frankish advances in Syria, and the death of al-Malik al-Muʿaẓẓam are described.
✧ In the year 626 AH, Jerusalem is surrendered to the Franks, Damascus changes hands among the Ayyubids, and Jalāl al-Dīn captures Khilāṭ.
✧ In the year 627 AH, Jalāl al-Dīn is defeated by Kayqubādh and al-Ashraf, and various territorial changes and rebellions occur.
✧ In the year 628 AH, the Tatars invade Azerbaijan and Diyār Bakr, Jalāl al-Dīn's power collapses, and notable deaths include Ibn Muʿṭī and al-Dakhwār.
✧ In the year 629 AH, administrative changes occur in Baghdad and Damascus, and a Tatar incursion into Shahrazūr is repelled by Muẓaffar al-Dīn of Irbil.
✧ Covers the investiture of Majd al-Dīn al-Manṣūrī, Ibn al-Jawzī's embassy to al-Kāmil, the conquest of Irbil, the building of the Ashrafiyya Dār al-Ḥadīth, and obituaries of prominent figures.
✧ Records the completion of the Mustanṣiriyya school and its endowments, diplomatic gifts to al-Ashraf, construction projects in Baghdad and Damascus, and obituaries of scholars and rulers.
✧ Mentions al-Mustanṣir's minting of silver dirhams, al-Ashraf's destruction of a sinful khān and building of the Mosque of Repentance, and deaths of Bahāʾ al-Dīn b. Shaddād and Ibn al-Fāriḍ.
✧ Relates al-Kāmil and al-Ashraf's repair of Byzantine damage, the Tatar threat, and obituaries including Ibn ʿUnayn, Ibn Diḥyah, and al-Ḥājirī with critical assessments of Ibn Diḥyah.
✧ Describes the Tatar siege of Irbil, al-Ṣāliḥ Ayyūb's employment of Khwarazmian troops, the rift between al-Ashraf and al-Kāmil, and obituaries of al-Malik al-ʿAzīz, Kayqubādh, and others.
✧ Narrates the deaths of al-Ashraf and al-Kāmil, the brief rule and surrender of al-Ṣāliḥ Ismāʿīl, the rise of al-Jawād in Damascus, and obituaries of al-Khaṭīb al-Dawlaʿī and others.
✧ Tells of al-Jawād's confiscations and exchange of Damascus for Ḥiṣn Kayfā with al-Ṣāliḥ Ayyūb, and obituaries of Jamāl al-Dīn al-Ḥaṣīrī and ʿImād al-Dīn b. Shaykh al-Shuyūkh.
✧ Details al-Ṣāliḥ Ismāʿīl's seizure of Damascus, the imprisonment and release of al-Ṣāliḥ Ayyūb, his accession in Egypt, and obituaries of Asad al-Dīn Shīrkūh and al-Qāḍī al-Khuwayyī.
✧ In 638 AH, al-Ṣāliḥ Ismāʿīl surrendered Shaqīf Arnūn to the Franks, provoking the imprisonment of two shaykhs, a Tatar envoy delivered a summons, and Muḥyī al-Dīn ibn ʿArabī died.
✧ In 639 AH, al-Malik al-Jawād fled toward Egypt but was arrested, al-Ṣāliḥ Ayyūb began building schools and a citadel in Egypt, and the ruler of Homs defeated the Khwarazmians at Ḥarrān.
✧ In 640 AH, the caliph al-Mustanṣir died and was succeeded by his son al-Mustaʿṣim, while the shrine at Samarra burned and a severe plague struck Iraq.
✧ In 641 AH, peace negotiations between al-Ṣāliḥ Ayyūb and his uncle al-Ṣāliḥ Ismāʿīl broke down, the Khwarazmians seized Rūm, and al-Qāḍī al-Rafīʿ al-Jīlī was killed.
✧ In 642 AH, al-Mustaʿṣim appointed Ibn al-ʿAlqamī as vizier, and the Khwarazmians, allied with al-Ṣāliḥ Ayyūb, inflicted a massive defeat on the coalition of Syrian Ayyubids and Franks near Gaza.
✧ In 643 AH, the Khwarazmians besieged Damascus, causing severe famine and death, before being defeated at the lake of Homs, and several prominent scholars died.
✧ In 644 AH, al-Manṣūr broke the Khwarazmians at the lake of Ḥimṣ, al-Ṣāliḥ Ayyūb entered Damascus and ordered the rebuilding of Jerusalem's walls, and a storm bared the Kaʿbah.
✧ In 645 AH, al-Ṣāliḥ Ayyūb returned to Egypt after conquering Tiberias and Ascalon, and notable deaths included the grammarian al-Shalūbīn and the controversial Shaykh ʿAlī al-Ḥarīrī.

✧ Covers Sultan al-Ṣāliḥ Ayyūb's return to Damascus, his illness and killing of his brother al-ʿĀdil, events in Damascus, deaths of Afḍal al-Dīn al-Khūnajī and Abū ʿAmr b. al-Ḥājib, and an account of Abū al-Ḥasan al-Mukharrimī.

✧ Records the death of Sultan al-Ṣāliḥ Ayyūb, the brief rule and killing of his son Tūrānshāh, the Frankish seizure of Damietta, and the rise of al-Muʿizz Aybak with the death of Fakhr al-Dīn b. al-Shaykh.
✧ Describes the recovery of Damietta from the Franks, the investiture of al-Muʿizz Aybak, the acquisition of Damascus by al-Nāṣir b. al-ʿAzīz, and biographies of al-Ṣāliḥ Ismāʿīl and Tūrānshāh.

✧ Details al-Nāṣir's return to Damascus, the marriage of Shajar al-Durr to Aybak, the transfer of al-Ṣāliḥ Ayyūb's coffin, destruction of Damietta, and deaths of Bahāʾ al-Dīn al-Jummayzī and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Lamghānī.
✧ Reports the Tatar raids on al-Jazira, the hajj from Baghdad, a fire in Aleppo, restoration of the Tājiyya Madrasa, and deaths of Jamāl al-Dīn b. Maṭrūḥ, ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz al-Maghribī, and others.

✧ Mentions the Aden fire, the killing of Aqṭāy, Shaykh ʿIzz al-Dīn b. ʿAbd al-Salām's teaching post, the marriage of the Roman king's daughter, and obituaries for al-Khusrūshāhī, Majd al-Dīn Ibn Taymiyya, and Kamāl al-Dīn b. Ṭalḥa.

✧ Describes the Hijaz earthquake and fire, the burning of the Prophet's Mosque, the completion of the Nāṣiriyya al-Juwāniyya school, and deaths including Sibṭ b. al-Jawzī and Sayf al-Dīn b. Abī al-Fawāris.

✧ Relates the deaths of ʿIzz al-Dīn Aybak and Shajar al-Durr, the accession of al-Manṣūr ʿAlī, sectarian strife in Baghdad, the Ḥaydarī fuqarāʾ entering Syria, and obituaries for al-Nāṣir Dāwūd, Ibn Abī al-Ḥadīd, and others.
✧ The Mongols under Hūlākū Qān captured Baghdad, massacred its inhabitants, and killed the last ʿAbbāsid caliph al-Mustaʿṣim, ending the dynasty in Iraq.
✧ Following the fall of Baghdad, Hūlākū advanced into Syria, capturing Mayyāfāriqīn and other strongholds while Quṭuz usurped the sultanate in Egypt.
✧ The Mongols seized Aleppo and Damascus, but Quṭuz defeated them at ʿAyn Jālūt; he was then assassinated and succeeded by Baybars al-Bunduqdārī.
✧ Baybars restored an ʿAbbāsid caliph with the brief investiture of al-Mustanṣir II and initially campaigned toward Iraq before the caliph was lost.
✧ Al-Mustanṣir II was killed, and al-Ḥākim bi-Amr Allāh was installed as caliph while Baybars consolidated control over Egypt and Syria.
✧ Baybars received oaths for al-Ḥākim, seized al-Karak, and dealt with the Tatar conflicts while appointing governors and judges across his realm.
✧ Building projects and appointments were carried out in Cairo and Damascus, and numerous scholars and officials died during this year.
✧ Baybars campaigned against the Franks, capturing Caesarea and Arsuf, while the Mamluk system of judges from all four legal schools was established in Egypt.
✧ Covers the appointment of four chief judges in Damascus, the conquest of Safad, and the raid on Sīs under Sultan al-Malik al-Ẓāhir.
✧ Details Sultan al-Ẓāhir's movements, restoration of the Azhar mosque, and deaths of Barakah Khān and al-Shaykh Abū Shāmah.
✧ Narrates the conquest of Antioch and Jaffa, conflicts with the Franks and Tatars, and notable deaths including Ibn Sabʿīn.
✧ Records Sultan al-Ẓāhir's renewed oath for his son, prohibition of wine, his Hajj, and deaths of amirs and scholars.
✧ Tells of the end of the Almohad dynasty, the capture of Misyāf, and the deaths of Ibn Abī Uṣaybiʿa and Ibn al-Zakī.
✧ Describes the campaigns against Ḥiṣn al-Akrād and Acre, the appointment of Ibn al-Ṣāʾigh, and deaths including Ibn Sabʿīn.
✧ Relates the sultan's campaigns, arrest of the Hanbali judge, and the deaths of al-Nawawī's teacher and others.
✧ Mentions the Nubian raid on ʿAydhāb, the handing over of Ismāʿīlī fortresses, and the deaths of notables.

✧ Reports the movements of al-Ẓāhir in Damascus in 672 AH, the completion of the Dayr al-Ṭīn mosque, and the obituaries of notables including Muʾayyid al-Dīn b. al-Qalānisī, Fāris al-Dīn Aqtāy, Ibn Mālik, and Naṣīr al-Dīn al-Ṭūsī.
✧ Chronicles al-Ẓāhir's campaign into Sīs against the Armenians in 673 AH and the obituaries of Ibn ʿAṭāʾ al-Ḥanafī and the Frankish count Baymūnd of Tripoli.
✧ Covers the Tatar siege of al-Bīrah, al-Ẓāhir's campaign against Dunqulah, disturbances at al-Karak, and the deaths of Tāj al-Dīn al-Ṣarkhadī, Ibn al-Ṣāʾigh, and Ibn al-Sāʿī.
✧ Describes the Battle of al-Bulustayn in 675 AH, al-Ẓāhir's conquest of Qaysariyyah, the wedding of al-Saʿīd, and the deaths of Ibn al-Fuwayrih and Shams al-Dīn al-Ḥarrānī.
✧ Narrates the deaths of al-Nawawī, al-Malik al-Qāhir, and al-Malik al-Ẓāhir in 676 AH, the succession of al-Saʿīd, and the obituaries of al-Barwānah, Bīlīk al-Khazindār, and others.

✧ Records the reinstatement of Ibn Khallikān as judge of Damascus in 677 AH, al-Saʿīd's entry into Damascus, and the obituaries of Āqūsh al-Najībī, Ṣadr al-Dīn Sulaymān, Ibn al-Ḥinnā, and Ibn Isrāʾīl al-Ḥarīrī.

✧ Describes the discord among the Ẓāhirī amirs in 678 AH, the deposition of al-Saʿīd, the accession of Qalāwūn as al-Manṣūr, Sunqur al-Ashqar's revolt in Damascus, and the deaths of Ibn Ghānim and al-Saʿīd.
✧ Relates the defeat of Sunqur al-Ashqar by al-Manṣūr's forces in 679 AH, the Tatar incursion into Syria, and the obituaries of Āqūsh al-Shamsī, Dāwūd al-Ḥabbāl, and the poet al-Jazzār.
✧ Covers the truce between the Sultan and ʿAkkā/al-Marqab, peace with Sunqur al-Ashqar, the Battle of Ḥimṣ against the Tatars, and the deaths of Abaqā and several scholars.
✧ Records the Tatar king Aḥmad's peace overture to al-Manṣūr, arrests of emirs, a fire in al-Labbādīn, and obituaries including Ibn Khallikān.
